title: Linguine al Granchio
subtitle: Crab, lemon, chilli, and pasta
excerpt: Linguine tossed with fresh white and brown crab meat, lemon, chilli, and a little good olive oil. Fast, light, and better than any restaurant version you can get in Britain without going to the coast.

recipe.sourceNotes: Pasta with crab is a staple of coastal Italian cooking, particularly in Puglia, Calabria, and the Venetian lagoon. The combination of brown and white crab meat, the brown for depth, the white for texture, is standard in authentic versions. The chilli and lemon are the sauce.

content.text: Linguine al granchio is one of the few pasta dishes where less is really more. The crab provides sweetness and a slight brininess; the chilli gives warmth; the lemon cuts through the richness; the olive oil binds it. Brown crab meat is stirred into the base of the sauce for depth; white meat goes in at the end so it stays in flakes rather than disappearing into the pasta.

items.preparation: white and brown, picked over for shell

content.text: Cook the pasta in well-salted boiling water. Reserve a large cup of pasta water before draining.
While the pasta cooks, heat the olive oil in a large frying pan over low-medium heat. Add the garlic and chilli and cook gently for 2 minutes until the garlic is softened but not coloured.
If you have brown crab meat, add it now and stir into the oil for 1 minute. Add a splash of pasta water to loosen.

Add the drained pasta and toss with the crab oil. Add the white crab meat, lemon zest and juice, and parsley. Toss together, adding a little more pasta water if the sauce looks dry. Season with salt and pepper.
Serve immediately. No cheese, crab and parmesan do not belong together.
